slide_details.Slide_Summary: DeepTek uses Isolation Forest for outlier detection, a method that identifies anomalies in data effectively.

slide_details.Text: Brief Introduction to Isolation forests DEEP They are similar to random forest in structure It performs random splits at each node instead of most informative split as used in random forest. Its basic principle is that outliers are very different from the rest of the data in terms of their features and hence Outliers are easy to isolate. easier to isolate By above assumption people have found out that they get classified at a very initial stage in the tree and so the length from the root node to its leaf node is considered to separate them. Inliers are harder to isolate Strictly Confidential Slide: 2
slide_details.Image Summary: The image is a diagram illustrating the relationship between outliers and inliers in a data set. The image is a diagram illustrating the difference in connectivity between outliers and inliers in a data set. It shows a tree-like structure with nodes connected by lines, where the outliers are represented as easier to isolate due to their distinct position in the structure.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Isolation forests are a type of algorithm that identifies outliers by making random splits at each node, allowing outliers to be easily isolated due to their distinct features. In contrast, inliers are more challenging to isolate within the data structure.

slide_details.Text: Al Needs Data . Al has shown fantastic results on a wide-range of tasks from object. detection to natural language processing.  Single most important factor that affects performance is the volume of data used for training.. . Deep learning is data hungry..
slide_details.Slide_Summary: AI performs well in various tasks, but its effectiveness largely depends on the amount of training data available, as deep learning requires a significant volume of data to achieve optimal results.

slide_details.Text: Data is Often Decentralized . Many valuable datasets are highly decentralized in nature.  Example: Datasets stored with different hospitals form data islands that are isolated from one another.  For conventional machine learning, all data must be moved to a central Iocation before training the models on it.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Many valuable datasets are decentralized, such as those stored in different hospitals, creating isolated "data islands." Conventional machine learning requires moving all data to a central location for model training.

slide_details.Text: Challenges in Data Movement : Data exists in different formats and needs to be marshalled into a common format before training . Data sources may be continuously collecting data. Centralization is not a one-time operation.  Communication costs may be prohibitive
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Data movement faces challenges due to varying formats that must be standardized for training, ongoing data collection from multiple sources, and high communication costs, making centralization an ongoing process rather than a one-time task.

slide_details.Text: Challenges in Maintaining Privacy. Regulations such as GDPR and HIPAA pose hurdles to movement of private data.  Organizations may not be comfortable sharing raw data of their users..
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Maintaining privacy is challenging due to regulations like GDPR and HIPAA, which restrict the movement of private data. Organizations often hesitate to share users' raw data because of these regulations.

slide_details.Image Summary: The image illustrates the Federated Learning Protocol, which is a process used in machine learning where multiple devices (like smartphones or servers) collaborate to train a model without sharing their local data. slide_details.Slide_Summary: Federated Learning allows multiple devices to collaboratively train a machine learning model without sharing their private data, ensuring privacy while reporting model updates to a central server. The server manages model checkpoints and handles device rejections as needed.

slide_details.Text: One Size Does Not Fit All. : Standard federated learning builds one global shared model for all clients. : Some of clients will have more data than others. Data distributions across clients are highly non-llD in practice..  In some cases, a local model using the client's private data may perform significantly better than the federated global model..  Clients that have very little data benefit the most. Clients that have sufficient data to train their own models have no incentive to participate..
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Standard federated learning creates a single global model for all clients, but clients often have varying amounts of data, leading to poor performance for some. Clients with little data benefit from this approach, while those with enough data may prefer to train their own models instead.

slide_details.Text: Personalization . This paper summarizes techniques used to personalize the global model for each client. and the global model.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The paper discusses methods for personalizing a global model for individual clients. It focuses on techniques that adapt the model to better meet the specific needs of each client.

slide_details.Text: 1. Adding User Context. . A shared global model can also produce highly personalized predictions if the client's context is featurized and incorporated into the dataset. . Can this be done without adversely affecting privacy?.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Incorporating user context into a shared global model can enhance personalized predictions, but it raises concerns about maintaining privacy.

slide_details.Text: 2. Transfer Learning . Transfer learning enables deep learning models to utilize the knowledge. gained in solving one problem to solve another related problem.. . Weights of the global model can used as initial weights for further training on local data. . Too much retraining can lead to catastrophic forgetting.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Transfer learning allows deep learning models to apply knowledge from one problem to a related problem by using the initial weights of a global model for further training on local data. However, excessive retraining may result in catastrophic forgetting of previously learned information.

slide_details.Text: 3. Multi-task Learning.  In multi-task learning, multiple related tasks are solved simultaneously allowing the model to exploit commonalities and differences across the tasks by learning them jointly.. : Smith et al. [2] show that multi-task learning is a natural choice to build personalized federated models and develop the MOcHA algorithm for. multi-task learning in the federated setting.. Since it produces one model per task, it is essential that all clients participate in every round..
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Multi-task learning involves solving multiple related tasks at the same time, enabling models to leverage similarities and differences among them. Smith et al. demonstrate its effectiveness for creating personalized federated models through the MOcHA algorithm, which requires participation from all clients in each round.

slide_details.Text: 4. Meta-Learning : Naively optimizing for global accuracy can hurt the model's ability for subsequent. personalization.  Goal is to find a highly adaptable global model that users can subsequently personalize on on local data. . This can be studied within the framework of Model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) [3]. : Fallah et al. [4] incorporate MAML and propose Per-FedAvg to find a global model that can be easily adapted.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Meta-learning aims to create a flexible global model that can be easily personalized with local data, rather than just optimizing for overall accuracy, which can hinder personalization. The approach is explored through Model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML), with Per-FedAvg being a proposed method to achieve this adaptability.

slide_details.Text: 5. Knowledge Distillation . Overfitting poses a significant challenge during personalization, especially for clients whose local dataset is small..  Knowledge distillation [6] involves compressing the knowledge of a large teacher network into a smaller student network by having the student mimic the teacher. . Yu et al. [5] propose that treating the global model as the teacher and the personalized model as the student, the effects of overfitting during. personalization can be mitigated.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Knowledge distillation helps reduce overfitting in personalized models by having a smaller student network learn from a larger teacher network. This approach treats the global model as the teacher and the personalized model as the student to improve performance, especially with small local datasets.

slide_details.Text: 6. Base + Personalization Layers. . Arivazhagan et al. [7] propose FedPer, a federated neural network. architecture.  The base layers are trained centrally by Federated Averaging. . The top layers (also called personalization layers) are trained locally with a variant of gradient descent.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide discusses FedPer, a federated neural network architecture proposed by Arivazhagan et al., where the base layers are trained centrally using Federated Averaging, while the top personalization layers are trained locally with a modified gradient descent approach.

slide_details.Text: Discussion . Most work in FL is focussed on measuring the performance of the global model on aggregated data instead of measuring its performance as seen by individual clients.  Global performance is irrelevant if the global model is expected to be subsequently personalized. : Future work - evaluate the above approaches for personalization and. benchmark results.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Most research in federated learning (FL) emphasizes the global model's performance on aggregated data rather than on individual clients, which is important for personalization. Future work should focus on evaluating personalization approaches and benchmarking their results.

slide_details.Text: Federated learning  E EF 1 - The clients download the current model from central server and improve it by updating their. model weights based on their local data. The client model parameter updates are aggregated to. generate server model. This model is again downloaded by the clients and the process continues.. 2 - No explicit sharing of raw data in this setup. 3 - Performance drops sharply when local data with clients is non i.i.d.. 4 - Data poisoning attacks on federated learning where malicious users can inject false training data to negatively affect the classification performance of the model have been proposed.. https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.04866 Strictly Confidential Slide: 6
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Federated learning allows clients to improve a central model using their local data without sharing it directly, but performance can decline with non-independent and identically distributed (non-i.i.d.) data. Additionally, there are risks of data poisoning attacks where malicious users can introduce false data to harm the model's performance.

slide_details.Text: Split learning.  E EP 1 - Each client trains the network upto a certain layer known as the cut layer and sends the weights to server. The server then trains the network for rest of the layers. This completes the forward propagation. Server then generates the gradients for the final layer and back-propagates the error until the cut layer. The gradient is then passed over to the client. The rest of the back-propagation is completed by client. This is continued till the network is trained.. 2 - Client-side communication costs are significantly reduced as transmitted data is restricted to first few layers of the SplitNN prior to split. 3 - It requires a relatively larger communication bandwidth when training over a small number of clients 4 - It's has no peeking properties.. Strictly Confidential Slide: 9
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Split learning involves clients training a neural network up to a designated cut layer and sending the weights to a server, which then completes the training and back-propagation. This method reduces client-side communication costs but requires more bandwidth when working with fewer clients and maintains confidentiality.

slide_details.Text: Overcoming the Challenges. We will use two approaches to overcome the challenges:  Time-window Synchronization: Identifying pulse in the data and synchronizing the time-window using the reference pulse  Time-synchronization using a common device: Using a common device to fire the transmitter as well as recording the ultrasonic signal using USB mic. slide_details.Slide_Summary: To overcome challenges, we will use two methods: synchronizing time-windows by identifying a reference pulse in the data, and using a common device to trigger the transmitter and record the ultrasonic signal.

slide_details.Text: Time-window Synchronization. Instead of considering 1 second chunks, we will consider the instance of the pulse and build a frame, starting a fixed milliseconds before the pulse and ending a fixed milliseconds after the pulse, and consider that as a chunk.. This will ensure that the signature of the pulse is in a fixed position (ideally. center) and the model is not trained on the position of the signature but the. differences in the signature for defective and normal poles.. 40 80500 Frame Frame considered considered 35 69000 keeping the  keeping the AMPLITUDE (dB) pulse in the pulse in the 30 57500 centre centre Frequency 46000 25 34500 20 23000 15 11500 10 50 5 Time Time Spectrogkaconsecond chunk Amplitude Vs eogrdph of 1 second chunk Asquared IoT

slide_details.Text: Summarization Definition: It is the process of shortening a text document with software, in order to create a summary with the major points of the original document. The main idea of summarization is to find a subset of data which contains the "information" of the entire set. Current System: The system picks up sample sentences which tries to cover all points mentioned in the documents. There is no weightage to any of the fields. Summarization in Legal domain: Both extractive and abstractive summarization can be tweaked to summarize the legal documents in a better way. Summary will be comprised of below points: Subject 3. Type of the case 4. Sections, Articles, Laws, Indian penal codes mentioned. 5. Historical Cases Referred.. 6. Brief summary for each of the event happened. 7. Case Status, Result of the case(appleat lost, fined 5oo0 rs, ...etc). Similar Problems solved by us:. 8. News article summarization.. 9. Headline Generation of news articles. 10. Extraction of Judgement from court case Hong Kong Jurisdiction. Best model was giving 80% accuracy. 2
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Summarization is the process of condensing a text document to highlight its main points, using software to select key sentences without prioritizing any specific information. In the legal domain, both extractive and abstractive methods can enhance the summarization of legal documents by including essential details such as case type, relevant laws, historical references, and case outcomes.

slide_details.Text: Clustering Definition: Document Clustering is a method for finding structure within a collection of documents, so that similar documents can be grouped into categories. In legal domain, similar case laws can be grouped together, which are having a similar context. This can be helpful for organizing documents and analyzing similar cases. Current system: 1. Considers entire document (case) for clustering irrespective of important fields (domain specific). 2. Works based on word frequency. Doesn't consider semantic meaning.. Improvements for Legal Domain 3.  Weightage can be provided to different fields for better results based on user's requirement such as sections, articles, judges etc E.g : For a query = 'kidnapping' with high weightage to "type of crime" field will result into something like below types clusters: Basic Kidnapping, High Net Worth Individual Kidnapping, Tiger Kidnapping, Express Kidnapping, Virtual Kidnapping, Political Kidnapping, Bride Kidnapping. 4.  Semantic models can be used to consider polysemy words(words with different meaning in different contexts). Same features can be used to create semantic clusters. 5. Legal sections such as laws, sections, acts, indian penal code's description can be used to improvise the clustering results. 3
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Document clustering organizes similar legal case laws into categories based on context, improving analysis and document management. Enhancements include assigning weight to specific fields and using semantic models to better capture meaning and context in clustering.

slide_details.Text: Important Keywords/Topics Extraction Definition: It is tasked with the automatic identification of terms that best describe the subject of a document. The identified phrases or words can be grouped together based semantic similarity to form the Topics. Current System: 1. Doesn't consider domain knowledge(other documents available in the domain) 2.  Important keywords are extracted based on occurrence based similarity with other words. Extract the words which are most similar to all the other words.. Improvements for Legal domain:. 3. The extracted keywords can be further classified into legal domain specific and case document specific. 4. A ranking algorithm can be applied to rank the keywords and represent them as per their class and rank. 5.This will give a better representation of the case document. A
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide discusses the automatic extraction of important keywords from documents, highlighting current limitations such as the lack of domain knowledge and reliance on word similarity. It suggests improvements for the legal domain, including classifying keywords and applying a ranking algorithm for better representation of case documents.

slide_details.Text: Named Entity Extraction Definition: Locates and classify named entity mentions in unstructured text into predefined categories such as the person names, organizations, locations, medical codes, time expressions, quantities, monetary values, percentages Current System: 1. Current system is trained to identify below named entities:. PERSON People, including fictional.e ORG Companies, agencies, institutions, etc. GPE Countries, cities, states.. LAW Named documents made into laws. LANGUAGE Any named language. DATE Absolute or relative dates or periods. TIME Times smaller than a day.. MONEY Monetary values, including unit.. 2. Current system is trained on news articles, so it makes some mistakes in identifies entities in legal domain Improvements for Legal Domain: We can improve current NER functionality specific to legal domain. Legal specific types of entities we can include judges, attorneys, companies, jurisdictions, and courts etc. 5

slide_details.Slide_Summary: Named Entity Extraction identifies and classifies entities in unstructured text into categories like people, organizations, and locations. The current system, trained on news articles, can be improved for the legal domain by including specific entities such as judges and attorneys.

slide_details.Text: Additional feature possibility - Coreference Definition : Coreference resolution is the task of identifying mentions in a text that refer to the same real-world entity. For example, the mentions "Obama", "the president", and "he" could all refer to Barack Obama. Coreference resolution is considered an important aspect of text understanding, and has numerous applications in real world applications. It can be used to find important references in legal documents, simplifying it and improving. its readability. Application : Coreference in legal domain examples :. Sri R.K. Jain, learned senior counsel appeared for Sri Prabhjot Singh. His client was arrested by police. Sri R.K. Jain, learned senior counsel appeared for Sri Prabhjot Singh. Sri R.K. Jain's client was arrested by police.. slide_details.Text: Our Understanding of the Problem  The client takes old computers and refurbishes them or destroys them. Data security of the hard drive is a major issue. The client wants to build a smart ccTV solution in which hard-disk related activity is detected and an alarm is raised. The most critical activity to identify is removal of hard disk from computer and what is done with it
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The client refurbishes or destroys old computers and is concerned about data security on hard drives. They want to create a smart CCTV system to detect hard drive removal and monitor its handling.

slide_details.Text: Our Proposed Solution  We will develop a real-time embedded Al system that consists of the following:. A deep learning model that is specifically trained on video inputs from client's work area to detect certain events  This model will use Video as input and will be a video analytics model  This model will be designed to run in real-time. A edge computing hardware system on which the above model will be embedded.  This system will reside in the work area of the client and will operate autonomously without external. intervention  A video camera that will act as the input sensor for the hardware system and the Al model.  A software application (with Ul) that issues alert to the designated person.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The proposed solution is a real-time embedded AI system that includes a deep learning model for video event detection, edge computing hardware for autonomous operation, a video camera for input, and a software application to send alerts.

slide_details.Text: Some Methods To Improve Performance  We moved from a three-class model approach to a two-tier two-class model approach, which seems to give a considerably better performance for classes saw-off and saw-on. Class 1 (saw-on-cut-off) vs class 2 (saw-on-cut-on) is still a challenge due to the. minority class problem (class 1 and class 2 are highly imbalanced). Earlier, there was less variation in the data available, which made the model fail in certain test-cases. We improved the variation in one of the machines, M7, by using Data Augmentation. This led to 20% increase in performance. However, this technique may or may not work for the other machines. That is yet to be seen. Asquared loT

slide_details.Text: Memory Networks The high-level view of a memory network is as follows: An input feature map I, which converts the incoming input to the internal feature representation A generalization component G which updates old memories given the new input. "We call this generalization as there is an opportunity for the network to compress and generalize its memories at this stage for some intended future use." An output feature map O, which produces a new output in the feature representation space given the new input and the current memory state A response component R which converts the output into the response format desired - for example, a textual response or an action.. A Memor I(x) I(x) O(Ix), G andano x qndu R Memory

slide_details.Slide_Summary: A memory network processes input through a feature map to create an internal representation, updates memories with new information, generates an output based on the current memory state, and converts that output into a desired response format. This structure allows the network to compress and generalize memories for future use.

slide_details.Text: Prob|em Context  Hospital orders medical supplies from various vendors. One item can be sourced from multiple vendors Item has a description, which is like concatenated word tokens about various attributes of the item. Later, when the hospital wants to search/compare/match these items, it requires the item attributes in structured pattern.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Hospitals order medical supplies from multiple vendors, and each item has a description made up of various attributes. To effectively search and compare these items later, the hospital needs these attributes organized in a structured format.

slide_details.Text: Solution and reference The item description strings can be matched when represented as vector assuming the attributes have meaningful representation, irrespective of their position in the string. This approach is popularly used in retail or ecommerce operations. It is known as product matching.. Item description is mapped in attributes [map phase], combine or arrange attributes [merge or structure phase]. This kind of approach is more closer to address delineation problem popularly used in logistic. industries.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide discusses a method for product matching in retail and e-commerce by representing item descriptions as vectors, allowing for meaningful comparison regardless of word position. This approach involves mapping item attributes and then structuring them, similar to techniques used in logistics for addressing delineation.

slide_details.Text: Technique Convolutional AutoEncoder architecture is used by training it on image data from normal class. It learns to reconstruct back the original image after compressing it to a lower dimension. Since information is passed through a small bottleneck, the model only learns to. reconstruct normal images and any image which is not from normal distribution is not reconstructed properly.. VGG-16 pre-trained on the huge dataset of ImageNet is used to encode the information into smaller dimension.. The objective function minimized during training is the pixel-wise MsE between input and reconstructed image. Image reconstruction is improved greatly by adding a VGG perceptual Ioss along with MSE during training : along with MSE, the distance between embeddings from a VGG ImageNet pre-trained model of input and reconstructed image is minimized, i.e. the model is learns to. After training, the anomaly score for a particular image is calculated by measuring similarity between input and reconstructed image. The metric here used is ssim index. Low similarity or low SSIM index indicates high abnormality in the image..
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The Convolutional AutoEncoder is trained on normal images to learn their reconstruction, using a VGG-16 model for encoding and minimizing pixel-wise MSE and perceptual loss. Anomaly detection is achieved by calculating the similarity between the input and reconstructed images, with low similarity indicating higher abnormality.

Logistic Regression: For each label (code or category), separate logistic regression model trained, and each one predicted the given label (0 or 1).. 2.  K-nearest neighbor: giving extra weights to keywords that provide diagnostic evidence in the document and using different parameters as distance metric.. 3.Bayesian classifiers 4. Feed Forward Neural Networks: Multi-label classification by setting up multiple neurons in the network output layer and each neuron represents a target label correspondingly.The ReLU activation function was utilized for all the hidden layers and sigmoid function was used for the output layer, binary cross entropy as the loss function, and stochastic gradient descent as the optimizer. no ith

slide_details.Text: STC Background Purpose: To find process drifts from preform core-deposition data and flag them for scrutiny. Data: DC1 data (from Waluj plant) ~6000 records per preform (across 21 stages)  42 data parameters (31 relevant parameters used for analysis) Method: Creating a model that looks at all parameters across all preforms and will be able to flag/point to specific parameters that are causing deviation A primary goal is to validate our approach of using PCA coefficients (used earlier), try to scale it, and look for other ways that may be more scalable.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The purpose of the STC project is to identify process deviations in preform core-deposition data from the Waluj plant by analyzing approximately 6,000 records across 21 stages. The project aims to develop a model that flags specific parameters causing deviations and to validate and potentially improve the use of PCA coefficients for this analysis.

slide_details.Text: STC Decision Points & Next Steps. Decision Points From recipe files, it appears that spindle-1 and spindle-2 have different parameters; hence we need to treat preforms coming. from different spindles separately. [validated by process expert] All approaches (PCA, overlay, recipe-vs-set-vs-actual) used should agree on what they point out as anomalous behaviour Next Steps See how this PCA based approach can be scaled and automated for large number of preforms. Complete the work on Recipe to Machine variation approach for LEB and REB variables.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The main points are that preforms from different spindles must be treated separately due to differing parameters, and all analysis methods should align on identifying anomalies. Next steps include scaling and automating the PCA approach for many preforms and finalizing the Recipe to Machine variation work for specific variables.

It details the methodology, including the use of PCA coefficients to identify process drifts and the comparison of recipe-based values with actual machine data. The next steps involve automating the PCA approach and addressing variations in recipes across different spindles to enhance process consistency and reliability.

slide_details.Text: Implementation Details Dataset Information Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) by Microsoft with FER+ labels were used. In FER+, each image has been labeled by 10 crowd-sourced taggers, which provide better quality ground truth for still image emotion. than the original FER labels. It is very imbalanced dataset containing approximately 36k images divided into train test and validation categories. Data Preparation  We have resized the images to particular fixed single dimension and used various data augmentation techniques like width. shift,height shift, zoom range, shear range, rotation.. We have also used featurewise_center as well as featurewise_std_normalization.. Model information We only train on 8 classes of the possible 10 given in fer+ i.e excluding the Not a Face and Unknown emotion classes  We have used vgg13 architecture with dropouts at various stages to make model robust and generalisable Results We are able to achieve accuracy of 82.73% on test dataset.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The study utilized the FER+ dataset for facial emotion recognition, which includes better quality labels from multiple taggers, and implemented data augmentation techniques on approximately 36,000 images. The VGG13 model, trained on 8 emotion classes, achieved an accuracy of 82.73% on the test dataset.

slide_details.Text: Major Challenges * GAN Problems: There are standard problems with GAN training as mentioned below: >  Non-convergence: The model parameters oscillate, destabilize and never converge. >Mode collapse: The generator collapses which produces limited varieties of samples. > Diminished gradient: The discriminator gets too successful that the generator gradient vanishes and learns nothing.  Problems which we are facing in GAN training: > Diminished gradient problem > Classification accuracy: The test samples are classified with a low probability. (in range from 0.47 to 0.53)  Object Detection and Semantic Segmentation Problems:  Input Image Semantic Segmentation Instance Segmentation >Initial Approach taken(Mask-RcNN) and Problems with it:  Mask R-CNN is suitable for Instance Segmentation When used for Semantic Segmentation it creates instance wise binary masks which in turn creates thousands of instances of a single class(chair), which is very memory intensive Final Approach: DeepLab model to perform Semantic Segmentation

slide_details.Text: Implementation Details Dataset Information Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) by Microsoft with FER+ labels were used. In FER+, each image has been labeled by 10 crowd-sourced taggers, which provide better quality ground truth for still image emotion. than the original FER labels. It is very imbalanced dataset containing approximately 36k images divided into train test and validation categories. Data Preparation  We have resized the images to particular fixed single dimension and used various data augmentation techniques like width. shift,height shift, zoom range, shear range, rotation.. We have also used featurewise_center as well as featurewise_std_normalization.. Model information We only train on 8 classes of the possible 10 given in fer+ i.e excluding the Not a Face and Unknown emotion classes  We have used vgg13 architecture with dropouts at various stages to make model robust and generalisable Results We are able to achieve accuracy of 82.73% on test dataset.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The project uses the FER+ dataset for facial emotion recognition, which includes 36,000 images labeled by multiple taggers for better accuracy. slide_details.Text: Problem statement  The amount of video footage being captured by cctv cameras is increasing everyday, and to monitor this. footage for anomalous activity like crime, accidents, etc takes manual human attention, and it is not possible for a person to monitor multiple feeds accurately. An algorithm which can be trained to detect anomalous activity will be highly applicable. We are focusing on. unsupervised algorithms which means that the training data need not be labelled. Our current is based on reconstructive modelling, which aims to create a hidden model of normalcy and then compare test data to model recreated data where anomalous events will stand out as the model cannot recreate anomalies accurately.  UcsD Dataset for Anomaly detection: Video captured from cameras overlooking pedestrian walkways in the University of California, San Diego. Contains 34 training and 36 test videos - training videos do not contain anomalies. Anomalies include: Cyclists, Vans, Skateboarders.  Pvt. Ltd 44

slide_details.Text: Results Object ROC AUC Accuracy Hazelnut 0.81 81 % Screw 0.70 71 % Toothbrushe 0.71 71 % Difficulties :  One of the main difficulty is that, for training purpose we only have good images of each class. Anomaly image data is only for testing purpose. To tackle this we tried isolation forest , OneClassSvM and autoencoder approach for anomaly classification task. To improve the results we have used patch strategy approach. In this we divide image into no of patches and use those patch for training and testing purpose. If one of patch is classified as anomaly for given test image then we will classify that image as anomaly else normal. slide_details.Text: Results Object ROC AUC Accuracy Hazelnut 0.81 81 % Screw 0.70 71 % Toothbrushe 0.71 71 % Difficulties : One of the main difficulty is that, for training purpose we only have good images of each class. Anomaly image data is only for testing purpose. To tackle this we tried isolation forest , OneClassSvM and autoencoder approach for anomaly classification task. To improve the results we have used patch strategy approach. In this we divide image into no of patches and use those classify that image as anomaly else normal. slide_details.Text: Caveats The results for gloss pipeline shown in the earlier slide were on a smaller test dataset. The original dataset has 105 NOK and 1000 OK images. The threshold for the models can be adjusted according to business decisions to include or exclude small defects.. Asquared loT

slide_details.Text: Post Localization Classifier (PLC) Since the Mask-RCNN model is good at identifying even the smallest of defects or artifacts, it will give us the regions of interest (ROl). slide_details.Text: NLP SIG How do people understand complicated concepts? It is by making analogies to the simpler concepts. This simpler thing is referred to as. common sense which contain knowledge about the world. It allows us to have reasonable conversation with other..  For example, If someone asks you whether a giraffe will be happy and comfortable in the room, you'll immediately have an answer without never thinking of this problem before. This is because you reach into your model of the world to understand what a giraffe is, how tall it is, and then you're inferring what that means for your specific space. If we want computers to be able to learn and generalize, we need to establish this base layer, which makes it possible for them to understand complicated concepts. Initial work in NLP lacks integration with the basic information about how the world works Retrofitting provides a way of connecting knowledge graphs to traditionally created word embeddings by pulling similar terms closer, and pushing different words farther. Photo by: Fir0002 CC BY-SA 3.0.  Numberbatch provides semantic vectors that can be used directly as a starting point for further ML. It is Built using an ensemble that combines data from ConceptNet, word2vec, GloVe, FastText using retrofitting tree oak furniture 0 2020 NTT DATA Corporation 13 NTT DaTa
slide_details.Slide_Summary: People understand complex concepts by relating them to simpler, common-sense knowledge about the world. For computers to learn and generalize effectively, they need a foundational understanding of this knowledge, which can be enhanced through methods like retrofitting that connect knowledge graphs to word embeddings.

slide_details.Text: NLP SIG Until 11/2018, almost all top-performing systems used retrofit. But BERT came, which changed many things. Transformers make key mistake when we interact with them. There is synergy between KG and transformer. Transformer has domain specificity, while KG can add common sense to the transformer. It is being researched by many: Transformers + Knowledge Graphs (https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07713) Transformers + ConceptNet (https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06725v1) Transformers + Entity Graphs (https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04164) Use a GAN to teach a network to add knowledge graph to an embedding (https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04163).  2020 NTT DATA Corporation 14 NTT DaTa
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Before BERT, most top NLP systems relied on retrofit, but BERT and transformers introduced new dynamics, highlighting the importance of combining transformers with knowledge graphs to enhance domain specificity and common sense reasoning. Ongoing research explores various integrations of transformers with knowledge graphs and related concepts.

slide_details.Text: NLP SIG How do people understand complicated concepts? It is by making analogies to the simpler concepts. This simpler thing is referred to as. common sense which contain knowledge about the world. It allows us to have reasonable conversation with other..  For example, If someone asks you whether a giraffe will be happy and comfortable in the room, you'll immediately have an answer without never thinking of this problem before. This is because you reach into your model of the world to understand what a giraffe is, how tall it is, and then you're inferring what that means for your specific space. If we want computers to be able to learn and generalize, we need to establish this base layer, which makes it possible for them to understand complicated concepts. Initial work in NLP lacks integration with the basic information about how the world works Retrofitting provides a way of connecting knowledge graphs to traditionally created word embeddings by pulling similar terms closer, and pushing different words farther. Photo by: Fir0002 CC BY-SA 3.0.  Numberbatch provides semantic vectors that can be used directly as a starting point for further ML. It is Built using an ensemble that combines data from ConceptNet, word2vec, GloVe, FastText using retrofitting tree oak furniture 0 2020 NTT DATA Corporation 13 NTT DaTa
slide_details.Slide_Summary: People understand complex concepts by relating them to simpler, common-sense ideas, which helps in reasoning and conversation. For computers to learn and generalize effectively, they need a foundational understanding of the world, which can be enhanced by integrating knowledge graphs with word embeddings through techniques like retrofitting.

slide_details.Text: NLP SIG Until 11/2018, almost all top-performing systems used retrofit. But BERT came, which changed many things. Transformers make key mistake when we interact with them. There is synergy between KG and transformer. Transformer has domain specificity, while KG can add common sense to the transformer. It is being researched by many: Transformers + Knowledge Graphs (https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07713) Transformers + ConceptNet (https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06725v1) Transformers + Entity Graphs (https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04164) Use a GAN to teach a network to add knowledge graph to an embedding (https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04163).  2020 NTT DATA Corporation 14 NTT DaTa
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Before BERT, most top NLP systems relied on retrofit, but BERT and transformers introduced new dynamics, highlighting the synergy between transformers and knowledge graphs (KGs) for enhancing domain specificity and common sense in NLP. Research is ongoing into combining transformers with various types of knowledge graphs to improve performance.

It keeps the RDS Instance running only during weekdays from 9am-5pm IST to save costs. CloudWatch Logs enables us to centralize the logs from all of our systems, applications, and AwS services that we use, in a single, highly scalable service. An S3 Lifecycle configuration is a set of rules that define actions that Amazon S3 applies to a group of objects. There are two types of actions Transition Actions and Expiration Actions. After the first day the objects will become non-current in this bucket. Only the 5 newest noncurrent versions are retained. All other noncurrent versions are permanently deleted. slide_details.Text: Some Methods To Improve Performance  We moved from a three-class model approach to a two-tier two-class model approach, which seems to give a considerably better performance for classes saw-off and saw-on. Classes saw-on-cut-off vs saw-on-cut-on still needs to be worked on as the accuracies are not meeting the target.  Class 1 (saw-on-cut-off) vs class 2 (saw-on-cut-on) is still a challenge due to the. minority class problem (class 1 and class 2 are highly imbalanced). As well as. the distinction between these classes is not as crisp as that of saw-off vs saw- on, and there is an overlap.  Earlier, there was less variation in the data available, which made the model fail in certain test-cases. We improved the variation in one of the machines, M7, by using Data Augmentation. This led to 20% increase in performance. However, this technique may or may not work for the other machines. That is yet to be seen. Asquared loT

Data augmentation on machine M7 increased performance by 20%, though its effectiveness on other machines is still uncertain.

Presentation_Summary: The presentation discusses the analysis and results of various AI modeling approaches applied to classify machine operations, transitioning from a three-class model to a two-tier two-class model to enhance performance. The initial three-class model faced challenges due to class imbalance, particularly with the minority class, leading to misclassification issues. The two-tier model showed improved accuracy, but further refinements are needed for distinguishing between closely related classes, with ongoing efforts in data augmentation and exploring advanced neural network techniques to boost performance.

slide_details.Text: Using pseudolabeling In competitions: - Label test set with your ensemble;. - Train new model; - Add it to the final ensemble In production: - Collect as much data as possible (both labeled and unlabeled); - Train model on labeled data;. - Apply pseudolabeling.

slide_details.Text: Instantaneous Fuel Consumption Asquared loT  Canonical problem for system efficiency metric that varies significantly and. non-linearly in real-time. : Instantaneous Fuel Consumption (km/l) varies significantly (from O when. idling to ~120 when "coasting" with no throttle input). .Varies with throttle input, engine RPM, engine load, vehicle speed, gradient of the road,. and many other parameters. Dataset with many different "regimes" - different behaviour in idling, low speed "crawling", city traffic, highway cruising and "coasting" etc.

slide_details.Text: Background: Multitasking / Specality DeepTek Radiologists are multitasking. Radiologists task is not standardized and the requirements also are not specific across centres. Example 1 A radiologist at a diagnostic centre working on health check-ups will need a radiologist skilled in doing Radiography, Mammography and Ultrasound of abdomen and pelvis. Example 2: A radiologist at a diagnostic centre working in association with a Obstetric and Gynecology hospital will need a radiologist skilled in doing Obstetric ultrasound.. Example 3: A radiologist at a diagnostic unit working in association with a Orthopedic Hospital will need radiologist skilled in doing MRI, CT and Color Doppler for peripheral vessels. In this hospital there may also be a need for a sub specialty trained radiologist who have skills in evaluating MSK images (MsK Radiologist). there may also be a need for a sub specialty trained radiologist who have skills in evaluating Neurology images (neuroradiologist). Example 5: A radiologist at a diagnostic Unit working in association with a Cancer Hospital will need radiologist skilled in doing Mammograms, MRI, CT and Ultrasound for staging purposes. They may also be a need for a sub specialty trained radiologist who have skills in evaluating mammogram images and body imaging respectively.. So the expertise of radiologists, their sub-specialty training carries a lot of value and there is a lot of "value-addition" in reports, unfortunately this is in short supply.. What if AI itself acts as the subspecialty trained radiologist who can assist trained radiologists in reporting to fill in those gaps. DeepTek Inc. | www.DeepTek.in | Confidential
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Radiologists often multitask and their required skills vary significantly across different healthcare settings, highlighting the need for specialized training. AI could potentially fill gaps in expertise by acting as a subspecialty-trained assistant to support radiologists in their reporting duties.

slide_details.Text: Case 2: Collection Analytics Collection analytics helps the debt collector or debt recovery processes to understand the behaviour of the customers, predicting their behaviour after default and directs the institution to prioritize collection activities to maximise recoveries and reduce costs. slide_details.Text: Decision Tree Decision tree builds classification or regression models in the form of tree structures. They are produced by algorithms that identify various ways of splitting a data set into branch like segments A decision node has tow or more branches. Leaf node represents a classification or decision.. The topmost decision node in a tree which corresponds to the best predictor called root node.. Each internal node is a test: - Theoretically, a node can test multiple attributes In most systems, a node tests exactly one attribute Each branch corresponds to test results -A branch corresponds to an attribute value or a range of attribute values The branches extending from a leaf node are decision branches, each branch representing one of the possible alternatives. The set of. alternatives must be mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.. Each leaf node assigns -a class: decision tree - a real value: regression tree  Page 7
slide_details.Slide_Summary: A decision tree is a model used for classification or regression that organizes data into a tree structure with decision nodes and leaf nodes. Each internal node tests an attribute, while leaf nodes represent classifications or values, with branches indicating possible outcomes.

slide_details.Text: The K-Means Clustering.  Given k, the k-means algorithm is implemented in four steps:. - Partition objects into k nonempty subsets. - Compute seed points as the centroids of the clusters of the current partition (the centroid is the center, i.e., mean point, of the cluster). - Assign each object to the cluster with the nearest seed point. - Go back to Step 2, stop when no more new assignment  Page 18
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The K-Means Clustering algorithm organizes data into k groups by repeatedly assigning objects to the nearest cluster center and updating the centers until no changes occur. It involves four main steps: partitioning, computing centroids, assigning objects, and iterating until stability is reached.

slide_details.Text: Introduction What is a BOT. Bot / Robot is an application that runs automated repetitive tasks over the Internet at a much higher rate than a human. Some bots are designed to be undetectable by mimicking human behavior. Bot Uses: -etchinq and analyzing tiles trom web servers Sending fast response in an online auction sites. Manipulating reviews in e-commerce websites. Committing fraud clicks on online advertisement. Co-ordinating automated attack on network computers.  Page 3
slide_details.Slide_Summary: A bot is an automated application that performs repetitive online tasks more quickly than humans, often mimicking human behavior to remain undetectable. Bots can be used for various purposes, including data analysis, manipulating online reviews, committing ad fraud, and launching coordinated cyber attacks.

slide_details.Text: CaClicktFraud as defined in Wikipedia "Click fraud occurs in pay per click online advertising when a person, automated script or computer program imitates a charge per click."  Google and yahoo faced lawsuits due to fraudulent clicks.. - Yahoo was sued by a class of advertisers who alleged Yahoo did not do enough to prevent click fraud. - The invalid clicks are done through bots to drive up advertisers' costs and eat up promotional budgets with - Yahoo paid $4.5 million in legal bills for the plaintiffs and agreed to settle advertiser claims. - Google settled a similar click fraud lawsuit with Lane's Gift and Collectibles for $90 million.  Page 4
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Click fraud involves fake clicks in online advertising that inflate costs for advertisers. Both Yahoo and Google faced lawsuits for not adequately preventing this issue, with Yahoo settling for $4.5 million and Google for $90 million.

slide_details.Text: CaOnline Auction Fraud : Following are most common fraud occurs in online auctions - Failure to ship merchandise - Failure to pay  - Shilling - Piracy and counterfeiting - Bogus Auctions  In eBay 65% of sessions are bot sessions. Bots are mainly used for. - Manipulating feedback form to get many positive reviews. - Placing bid faster than human, raise the bidding price or win the auction. - Hacking trust worthy seller's account and start a bogus auction.  Page 5
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Common online auction frauds include failure to ship or pay for items, shilling, piracy, and bogus auctions. Additionally, 65% of eBay sessions are bots, which manipulate feedback, place bids quickly, and hack accounts to create fake auctions.

slide_details.Text: Business Value Business Value Bot detection models should never rely on any static signatures or fixed rules. Machine learning models helps to. Classify each bidder/bot session based on features derived from historical behavior data Constantly self tune the model to evolve alongside the morphing threats.  Page 6
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Bot detection models should use machine learning instead of static signatures or fixed rules, allowing them to classify bidders based on historical behavior and continuously adapt to changing threats.

slide_details.Text: Stock Prediction: An introduction  Stocks  The most popular category of financial instruments What about prediction of stocks?  Generally believed to be a difficult/impossible task. slide_details.Text: Common viewpoints  The Efficient Market Hypothesis. slide_details.Text: S XX Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). N L P Generative Find parameters to maximize P(X,Y) Assumes features are independent. When labeling X, future observations are taken into account (forward-backward)
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) are generative models used in natural language processing to find parameters that maximize the probability of observed data and labels. They assume feature independence and consider future observations when labeling data.

slide_details.Text: S MaxEnt Markov Models (MEMMs N L P Discriminative Find parameters to maximize P(Y(X) No longer assume that features are independent. Do not take future observations into account (no forward- backward)
slide_details.Slide_Summary: MaxEnt Markov Models (MEMMs) are a type of discriminative model that optimize parameters to maximize the probability of output given input, without assuming feature independence or considering future observations.

slide_details.Text: S Conditional Random Fields (CRFs). N L P Discriminative Doesn't assume that features are independent When labeling Y, future observations are taken into account > The best of both worlds!.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) are a type of discriminative model used in natural language processing that do not assume feature independence and consider future observations when labeling, combining advantages of different approaches.

slide_details.Text: (C) Vipin Kumar, CSci 5980 Data Mining, Spring 2004. Definition: Frequent Itemset PERSISTENT Itemset A collection of one or more items. > Example: {Milk, Bread, Diaper} k-itemset TID Items > An itemset that contains k items 1 Bread, Milk Support count (o) 2 Bread, Diaper, Beer, Eggs  Frequency of occurrence of an itemset. 3 Millk, Diaper, Beer, Coke - E.g. o({Milk, Bread,Diaper}) = 2 4 Bread, Milk, Diaper, Beer . Support 5 Bread, Milk, Diaper, Coke - Fraction of transactions that contain an ite. -E.g. s({Milk, Bread, Diaper}) = 2/5 .Frequent Itemset An itemset whose support is greater than or equal to a minsup threshold. 44
slide_details.Slide_Summary: A frequent itemset is a collection of items that appears in transactions with a frequency above a specified minimum support threshold. For example, an itemset like {Milk, Bread, Diaper} is considered frequent if it occurs in a significant portion of the transactions.

slide_details.Text: (C) Vipin Kumar, CSci 5980 Data Mining, Spring 2004 Definition: Association Rule PERSISTENT Association Rule TID Items An implication expression of the form X 1 Bread, Milk and Y are itemsets 2 Bread, Diaper, Beer, Eggs Example: {Milk, Diaper} ->{Beer} 3 Milk, Diaper, Beer, Coke 4 Bread, Milk, Diaper, Beer Rule Evaluation Metrics 5 Bread, Milk, Diaper, Coke -Support (s)  Fraction of transactions that contain both X and Y Confidence (c) Example: > Measures how often items in Y Milk , Diaper = Beer appear in transactions that contain X o (Milk ,Diaper,Beer) (Milk,Diaper,Beer) o(Milk, Diaper) 3 45
slide_details.Slide_Summary: An association rule is a relationship between itemsets, expressed as X -> Y, where X and Y are groups of items. Key metrics for evaluating these rules include support, which measures the fraction of transactions containing both X and Y, and confidence, which indicates how often items in Y appear in transactions that include X.

slide_details.Text: (C) Vipin Kumar, CSci 5980 Data Mining, Spring 2004 Association Rule Mining Task PERSISTENT  Given a set of transactions T, the goal of association rule mining is to find all rules having  support  minsup threshold - confidence  minconf threshold Brute-force approach:  List all possible association rules Compute the support and confidence for each rule -Prune rules that fail the minsup and minconf thresholds - Computationally prohibitive! 46
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Association rule mining aims to identify rules from a set of transactions based on minimum support and confidence thresholds. slide_details.Text: Signature Verification - Error Categories. False Positives . Signatures are visually different but system gives high confidence score. Hence, shows match..  Type 1: Signatures are visually very different, from different. signers authors but are visually close. False Negatives  Signatures are visually close but system gives low confidence score. Hence, shows mismatch.. but different in visual style, yet humans say it is a match.. Type 2: Random : Signatures are close / identical..   Pvt. Ltd. | Page 20
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide discusses error categories in signature verification, highlighting false positives where visually different signatures are incorrectly matched, and false negatives where visually similar signatures are incorrectly mismatched. It also mentions a random category for signatures that are close or identical.

slide_details.Text: Post Localization Classifier (PLC) Since the Mask-RCNN model is good at identifying even the smallest of defects or artifacts, it will give us the regions of interest (ROl). These ROls include actual defects, small artifacts that are not big enough to be classified as. defect, reflections, defects in background, masking tape defects and false positives.  These ROls are cropped out and a separate Resnet 101 classification model is trained on these. images This model will determine if the ROl is an actual defect or not This should keep the Recall high and give us control over deciding if the small faults (dust etc.). are of relevance or not. slide_details.Slide_Summary: The Post Localization Classifier (PLC) uses a Mask-RCNN model to identify regions of interest (ROIs) related to defects and artifacts, which are then analyzed by a Resnet 101 model to classify them as actual defects or not, helping maintain high recall and assess the relevance of minor faults.

slide_details.Text: Pipeline: Mask-RCNN + PLC Pipeline: The process of tying together multiple models. In our case we first pass the images through Mask-RCNN model and. generate ROls. slide_details.Text: Detection of Air Leakage in Industrial Setting  Leakage of compressed air from pneumatic machines and lines is a. common problem in manufacturing industry : Unlike some other gases, air is odourless and colourless  Makes it very hard. to detect leakage of compressed air. . Leakage of compressed air can have significant effect on the performance of the pneumatic equipment. . Not easy to hear for humans due to high background noise in the factory  We use Sound Analytics models to detect leakage of compressed air. in factories . Our models work accurately even in the presence of background noises! . Example: For a MNc client, we detected leakage of air from pneumatic. fixtures in their ultrasonic welding machine!
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Compressed air leakage in industrial settings is difficult to detect due to its odorless and colorless nature, as well as high background noise. Sound Analytics models can effectively identify these leaks, even in noisy environments, improving the performance of pneumatic equipment.

slide_details.Text: Classification Results on Air Leakage. slide_details.Text: Problem statement  Now a days fashion industry shifting towards online and virtual outfits trying Goal of project is with given a reference image of a person and a target cloth , CP-VTON is to synthesize. a new image of the wearer in the new cloth , in which the body shape and pose of reference image are. retained, the characteristics of target clothes are reserved and the effects of the old clothes are eliminated. For this we used variation of GAN as CP-VTON.  Pvt. Ltd 65
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The project aims to create a new image of a person wearing a target outfit by using a reference image, while maintaining the person's body shape and pose, preserving the target clothing's features, and removing the old outfit. This is achieved through a variation of Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) called CP-VTON.

slide_details.Text: Approach CP-VTON contain 2 main module o  Geometric Matching Module: The in-shop clothes c and input image representation p aligned via a learnable. matching module. O Try-On Module: It generates a competition mask M and a rendered person I,. The final results I. is composed by wrapped cloths c and render person with the composite mask.  Pvt. Ltd 66

slide_details.Slide_Summary: CP-VTON consists of two main modules: a Geometric Matching Module that aligns clothes with an input image, and a Try-On Module that creates a composition mask and combines the aligned clothes with a rendered person. This process enables realistic virtual try-ons by generating a composite image.

slide_details.Text: Training and Evaluation The model is trained for 150 epochs using stochastic gradient descent with momentum of. 0.9, an initial learning rate of 8 x10-3, and a decay of 0.99 after every epoch. The Chebyshev convolutions use K = 4. An L2-weight decay with strength 2 x 10-3 is used. as regularization. Batch normalization is not used in our network. as we noticed that it Ieads to unstable training. Typical evaluation metrics for generative models such as Inception Score and FiD are not. available for 3D meshes. Therefore, we evaluate our model's representation power by. computing the per-vertex Euclidean auto-encoding error on clothing meshes..  Pvt. Ltd 7 1

slide_details.Text: Evaluation Method (U-NET) U-Net is a convolutional neural network that was developed for biomedical image segmentation. The network is based on the fully convolutional network and its architecture was modified and extended to work with fewer training images and to yield more precise segmentations. The network consists of a contracting path and an expansive path, which gives it the u- shaped architecture. The contracting path is a typical convolutional network that consists of repeated pooling operation. During the contraction, the spatial information is reduced while feature information is increased. The expansive pathway combines the feature and spatial information through a sequence of up-convolutions and concatenations with high-resolution features from the contracting path.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: U-Net is a convolutional neural network designed for biomedical image segmentation, featuring a u-shaped architecture with a contracting path to reduce spatial information and an expansive path to combine features and spatial data for precise segmentations. It is optimized to work effectively with fewer training images.

The network is based on the fully convolutional network and its architecture was modified and extended to work with fewer training images and to yield more precise segmentations. The network consists of a contracting path and an expansive path, which gives it the u- shaped architecture. The contracting path is a typical convolutional network that consists of repeated pooling operation. During the contraction, the spatial information is reduced while feature information is increased. The expansive pathway combines the feature and spatial information through a sequence of up-convolutions and concatenations with high-resolution features from the contracting path.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: U-Net is a convolutional neural network designed for biomedical image segmentation, featuring a U-shaped architecture with a contracting path to reduce spatial information and an expansive path to combine feature and spatial information for precise segmentations. It is optimized to work effectively with fewer training images.

slide_details.Text: Introduction Research Talent Industry  Politics  Predictions #stateofai Definitions intelligence that is demonstrated by humans and animals. It has become a somewhat catch all term that nonetheless captures the Iong term ambition of the field to build machines that emulate and then exceed the full range of human cognition. Machine Iearning (mL): A subset of Al that often uses statistical technigues to give machines the ability to "learn" from data without being explicitly given the instructions for how to do so. This process is known as "training" a "model" using a learning "'algorithm" that progressively improves model performance on a specific task. Reinforcement Iearning (RL): An area of ML concerned with developing software agents that learn goal-oriented behavior by trial and error in an environment that provides rewards or penalties in response to the agent's actions (called a "policy") towards achieving that goal. Deep learning (DL): An area of ML that attempts to mimic the activity in layers of neurons in the brain to learn how to recognise complex patterns in data. The "deep" in deep learning refers to the large number of layers of neurons in contemporary ML models that help to learn rich representations of data to achieve better performance gains. stateof.ai 2020

slide_details.Text: #stateofai Definitions Algorithm: An unambiguous specification of how to solve a particular problem.. Model: Once a ML algorithm has been trained on data, the output of the process is known as the model. This can then be used to make predictions. Supervised Iearning: A model attempts to learn to transform one kind of data into another kind of data using labelled examples This is the most common kind of ML algorithm today. Unsupervised Iearning: A model attempts to learn a dataset's structure, often seeking to identify Iatent groupings in the data without any explicit labels. The output of unsupervised learning often makes for good inputs to a supervised learning algorithm at a later point. problem, thereby reducing the need for significant additional training data and compute.. Natural Ianguage processing (nlP): Enabling machines to analyse, understand and manipulate language.. Computer vision: Enabling machines to analyse, understand and manipulate images and video. stateof.ai 2020

slide_details.Text: Technique Convolutional AutoEncoder architecture is used by training it on image data from normal class. It learns to reconstruct back the original image after compressing it to a lower dimension. Since information is passed through a small bottleneck, the model only learns to. reconstruct normal images and any image which is not from normal distribution is not reconstructed properly.. VGG-16 pre-trained on the huge dataset of ImageNet is used to encode the information into smaller dimension.. The objective function minimized during training is the pixel-wise MsE between input and reconstructed image. Image reconstruction is improved greatly by adding a VGG perceptual Ioss along with MSE during training : along with MSE, the distance between embeddings from a VGG ImageNet pre-trained model of input and reconstructed image is minimized, i.e. the model is learns to. After training, the anomaly score for a particular image is calculated by measuring similarity between input and reconstructed image. The metric here used is ssim index. Low similarity or low SSIM index indicates high abnormality in the image..
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The Convolutional AutoEncoder is trained on normal images to learn their reconstruction, using a VGG-16 model for encoding and minimizing pixel-wise MSE and perceptual loss. Anomaly detection is achieved by calculating the similarity between the input and reconstructed images, with low similarity indicating abnormalities.

slide_details.Text: Memory Networks The high-level view of a memory network is as follows: An input feature map I, which converts the incoming input to the internal feature representation A generalization component G which updates old memories given the new input. "We call this generalization as there is an opportunity for the network to compress and generalize its memories at this stage for some intended future use." An output feature map O, which produces a new output in the feature representation space given the new input and the current memory state A response component R which converts the output into the response format desired - for example, a textual response or an action.. Distorted reconstruction for anomalous region. Usable with prediction and reconstruction. Semi Supervised  Utilization of anomalous data available in small quantity for training.  Entropy of latent for normal data is lower than that for anomalous data. slide_details.Text: Detailed limitations of the Prompt Optimizer Agent (1/2) (for reference) 1. Not always needed: If the input is already clear and well-structured, optimizing it doesn't add much value.. a. Ex: "Query: I want a increase sales for [product] within [date] with budget [budget] ". Slower responses: The extra step of refining prompts can slow things down, which isn't ideal for real-time or fast-paced environments. 3. Limited scope of optimization: It can only refine the prompt by expanding its scope or making it clearer but cannot add entirely new insights a. Ex: "Query: How to increase sales strategy?". slide_details.Slide_Summary: The Prompt Optimizer Agent may not be necessary for clear inputs, can slow down response times, has a limited ability to enhance prompts without adding new insights, and does not utilize external information for optimization.

Hard to maintain: Keeping prompt and response templates up to date can be time-consuming and prone to errors, especially when requirements change. a.  Ex: Template for a documentation may change every month thus needing to update it every time 7. Depends on the Al model: If the foundation model itself isn't great at handling certain queries, the optimizer might not be able to fix everything a. Ex: "Query: How to increase sales strategy?". Here, OpenAl GPT might give a different output compared to Llama. 8.  Not ideal for long conversations: While it helps improve single questions, keeping the context consistent across multiple exchanges can be challenging without a strong memory system. a. slide_details.Text: Benefits & Drawbacks (As per the Research Paper) Benefits:  Efficiency: The agent can generate a plan to achieve users' goals by querying the underlying foundation model only once, which saves consumed time. Cost-efficiency: Users' expenses can be reduced since the foundation model is queried for one time.. Simplicity: One-shot model querying can satisfy the tasks that do not require complex action plans.. Drawbacks: Oversimplification: For complex tasks, one-shot model querying may not be able to fully capture all requirements at one time, hence oversimplifying the tasks and cannot return a correct response. slide_details.Slide_Summary: The research paper highlights that one-shot querying of a foundation model offers benefits like efficiency, cost savings, and simplicity for straightforward tasks, but it also has drawbacks such as oversimplification of complex tasks, lack of explainability, and limitations due to context window size.

slide_details.Text: Detailed limitations of the Multimodal Guardrails(1/2) (for reference) 1. Lack of Explainability - Opaque Decision-Making: Multimodal guardrails work using complex models (e.g., deep learning classifiers, NLP-based content filtering), which often lack transparency in decision-making. Users may not understand why their input was blocked or modified. If a guardrail rejects a valid query or flags an innocent response as inappropriate, users may lose trust in the system and find it frustrating. Ex: A user asks: "Does the iPhone 15 have overheating issues?" If the system mistakenly flags the word "issues" as negative or toxic, it might block the question unfairly. Since the user does not receive an explanation, they might assume the chatbot is biased or unreliable. 34
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The main limitation of multimodal guardrails is their lack of explainability, as complex models can make opaque decisions that frustrate users when valid inputs are blocked or modified without clear reasoning. This can lead to a loss of trust in the system if users feel their queries are unfairly flagged.

slide_details.Text: Detailed limitations of the Multimodal Guardrails(2/2) (for reference). 2. Ex: A chatbot designed for Apple mobile products needs to process images of phone models to confirm whether a user is asking about an iPhone. slide_details.Text: Key Findings from the Research Work:. In the context of the edge computing spectrum and generative Al, we explored solutions with respect to Device Edge and Compute Edge, particularly those offered by NVIDIA, which are designed to support generative Al applications NVIDiA website has tutorial repository where Generative Al applications across modalities (text, image, audio) have been implemented for demo purpose. This repository was helpful in understanding the different aspects of deploying Gen Al on Edge.. Parameter Performance Trade-off: Higher parameter models perform slower, a trade-off has to be made between complexity and speed while selecting the hardware and model. AGX Orin for Real-Time: Through the benchmarking done by NVIDIA for VLMs on their edge devices, we found that AGX Orin's higher FPS rates and. better performance suggest better suitability for real-time Gen Al applications. Meanwhile smaller edge device models like Orin Nano faced memory limitations with larger models (OoM errors). Through this project, we explored several open-source SLMs, including multimodal SLMs (VLMs), which have enormous potential in manufacturing. domain. We also found tools and frameworks to run open-source Gen Al models locally, such as Ollama and TinyChat (From MIT-HAN labs). NTT DaTa
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The research focused on NVIDIA's solutions for deploying generative AI applications at the Device Edge and Compute Edge, highlighting the trade-off between model complexity and performance. It identified the AGX Orin as optimal for real-time applications, while smaller devices like Orin Nano faced memory limitations, and explored various open-source models and tools for local implementation.

slide_details.Slide_Summary: Federated learning (FL) allows AI models to be trained using data from multiple sources without exposing the data itself, enhancing privacy and enabling applications like voice recognition and healthcare. This approach improves model robustness and personalization while keeping data secure and localized.

slide_details.Text: Types of Federated Learning Settings (HFL & VFL) Horizontal Federated Learning (HFL)  In HFL, the data is considered to be horizontally partitioned  It is ideally used in a scenario where the participating organizations hold data with similar feature sets RIVACY-ARESERVING Eg., Multiple Hospitals participating in an FL study can train their personalized Cancer Detection model using CT-scans from different set of patients NOPERSONANGED  The motivation of HFL is to make local inferences considering the influence of global data patterns (without data sharing). Vertical Federated Learning (VFL)  In VFL, the data is considered to be vertically partitioned  It is ideally used in a scenario where the participating organizations hold data with overlapping samples but different feature RIVACY-ARFSERVIN sets Eg., A Bank and an Insurance Org. participating in an FL study can train a Fraud Detection  Model using personal financial information as well as credit scores of an individual  The motivation of VFL is to make a robust global model that can infer by utilizing the data being lend by multiple parties. 3 (without data sharing) O
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Federated Learning has two main types: Horizontal Federated Learning (HFL), where organizations with similar features share insights without sharing data, and Vertical Federated Learning (VFL), where organizations with overlapping samples but different features collaborate to create a robust model while maintaining data privacy.

slide_details.Text: Key Learnings Federated Learning 1. There are 2 settings of incorporating Federated Learning (Horizontal FL and Vertical FL) a. HFL is ideally used when participating organizations share the same data features Eg., Multiple Hospitals participating in FL study to train a Cancer Detection model b. VFL is ideally used when participating organizations share the same data samples with common IDs Eg., A Bank and an Insurance Org. participating in FL study to train a Fraud Detection model 2. Federated Learning helps preserve data privacy at the cost of increased model learning time 3. In VFL, common IDs between local data from participating organizations are identified using a secure algorithm called Private Set Intersection (PSI) Frameworks 4. Hands-on experience in VFL with FATE framework with in-depth understanding of FATE's architecture 5. Preliminary hands-on experience in VFL with NVFlare framework 6. Knowledge of designing components as well as modifying source code for customised problem statements O  13
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Federated Learning has two main types: Horizontal FL, used when organizations share the same data features, and Vertical FL, used when they share the same data samples with common IDs. It enhances data privacy but may increase model training time, and involves secure algorithms like Private Set Intersection for identifying common IDs.

Key objectives include evaluating various VFL frameworks, particularly FATE and NVFlare, through extensive literature reviews, hands-on experimentation, and performance comparisons, while emphasizing the importance of data privacy and the technical processes involved in federated learning. The findings highlight the distinct applications of Horizontal and Vertical Federated Learning, the significance of secure algorithms like Private Set Intersection, and the trade-offs between data privacy and model learning efficiency.

Objective Statistical properties of a text corpus refer to the patterns and relationships found in written language. The main objective of LLMs is To generate new text that resembles human-written. These properties include how often words are used, which words go together, and how sentences are. content structured. By learning the patterns, grammar, and context from. the text corpus, LLMs can generate coherent and. contextually relevant sentences, paragraphs, or even. Computers can learn from these patterns to generate new text that sounds like it was written by a. longer passages of text.  person. NOTE: While statistical probabilities are not explicitly used in LLMs, the training process involves. optimizing the model's parameters to capture the statistical properties of the data indirectly..
