slide_details.Text: Flowchart for Pseudo Query Generation: Start: Begin with the original dataset containing query-document pairs. Combination with Another Document: For each query-document pair, combine the document with another document in a similar context.. Example: Original pair - (Query: "What is the capital of France?", Document: "Paris is the capital...").. for its history..."). Input to LLM (GPT-3): Present the combined query-document pairs to a Large Language Model (LLM), such as GPT-3.. Query Generation: The LLM generates various queries based on the combined document pairs. Example: Generate queries like "Tell me about the history of Paris" or "what are the attractions in Paris?'. Filtering with Fine-Tuned Model: Use a fine-tuned model (e.g., monoT5-3B) to filter and keep the top pairs with the highest estimated relevance scores. This helps in selecting high-quality synthetic samples. Iterative Loop (Optional): Optionally, the generating-then-filtering process can be conducted iteratively, refining the quality of synthetic samples. End: The final set of filtered query-document pairs can be used for training retrieval models.
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide outlines a process for generating pseudo queries by combining original query-document pairs with similar documents, using a Large Language Model (LLM) to create new queries, and filtering the results with a fine-tuned model to select high-quality samples for training retrieval models. An optional iterative loop can further refine the quality of the generated queries.

slide_details.Text: Flowchart for Relevance Label Generation:. Start: Begin with the original dataset containing questions and passages. Top-Relevant Passages Retrieval (ART Method): Use the ART method to retrieve top-relevant passages for each question. Example: For the question "what is the capital of France?" retrieve the passage containing information about Paris being the capital. Input to LLM (e.g., GPT-3): Present the combination of question and top-relevant passages to an LLM.. Label Generation:. The LLM generates probabilities indicating the relevance of the question to each top-relevant passage.. Example: Probabilities like [0.8, 0.2], where 0.8 indicates high relevance to the first passage and 0.2 to the second. Normalization Process:. Normalize the generated probabilities to create soft relevance labels.. Example: Normalize [0.8, 0.2] to get a distribution like [0.8, 0.2].. Training Retriever Models: Use these soft relevance labels as training data to train retriever models.. This process enhances the model's understanding of the relevance between questions and passages. End: The trained retriever models can be used for improved retrieval in question-answering tasks..
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide outlines a process for generating relevance labels by retrieving top-relevant passages for questions using the ART method, presenting them to a language model to generate relevance probabilities, normalizing these probabilities into soft relevance labels, and using them to train retriever models for better question-answering performance.

slide_details.Text: We gave client to choose between two options and their team had one proposal from their side too: 1. LLM based data extraction workflow. 2.  Azure Document Analysis based workflow for data extraction. 3. Xerox based data extraction workflow(their team proposal) After discussion we went with Azure Document Intelligence as the final choice Now, summary of what we did during the whole project O 2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The client chose the Azure Document Intelligence workflow for data extraction after considering two other options, including a proposal from their team. The summary reflects the project's progress under NTT DATA Corporation in 2023.

slide_details.Text: Initial Approach: OpenAl-Powered Pipeline Python pipeline using OpenAl API Deployed on Aws using Aws Apprunner services to be used in Dify High text accuracy (~99%) Metadata and structure captured well Issues with merged cells and minor Japanese text error Avg processing time: 2-4 mins/file  2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The initial approach involves a Python pipeline powered by OpenAI, deployed on AWS using App Runner, achieving high text accuracy of about 99%. It processes files in 2-4 minutes but faces issues with merged cells and minor errors in Japanese text.

slide_details.Text: Deployment architecture:. AWS Apprunner PDF file to Images Images sent to LLM for. Conversion of office file (.docx or .xlsx) into PDF format using libreoffice extraction Concatenation of each page. extraction File Upload Output text in Markdown format Dify Workflow  2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide outlines a deployment architecture using AWS Apprunner to convert office files (.docx or .xlsx) into PDF format with LibreOffice, followed by extracting and concatenating the pages into Markdown format.

slide_details.Text: Client requested experimentation with other tools for comparison and explorations:. So we explored and proposed Azure Document Intelligence. Their team proposed zerox API: 1. Zerox API- Easy integration but limited control. 2. Azure Document Intelligence - Strong layout understanding and markdown support. We tested the results from the initial OpenAl approach, Xerox API and Azure Document Intelligence Decided to move with Azure Document Intelligence.. O 2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The client explored different tools for document processing and compared the Xerox API, which offers easy integration but limited control, with Azure Document Intelligence, which has strong layout understanding and markdown support. They decided to proceed with Azure Document Intelligence based on their testing results.

slide_details.Text: Why Azure Document Intelligence? Azure Doc Intelligence with Prebuilt Layout Model. Outputs in Markdown format directly from model preserving structure Even flowchart text was extracted from the document with 100% accuracy. Better handling of Japanese text and table structures.  2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: Azure Document Intelligence offers a Prebuilt Layout Model that accurately extracts text and structures from documents, including flowcharts and Japanese text, and outputs the results in Markdown format.

slide_details.Text: Deployment architecture: AwS Apprunner Analysing of document using Azure doc Int Conversion of office file (.docx or .xlsx). prebuilt-layout model and output in. into PDF format Markdown format in FastAPI Response. File Upload Output text in Markdown format. Dify Workflow   2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide outlines a deployment architecture using AWS App Runner and Azure for analyzing documents, converting Office files (.docx or .xlsx) into PDF and Markdown formats, and delivering the output through a FastAPI response. It also mentions a file upload feature and a Dify workflow.

slide_details.Text: Other methods tested during the initial sprints but were not giving results as expected: PaddleOCR . TesseractOcR Markitdown. openpyxl PyMuPDF . Extraction of Japaneses text using Langchain and mecab  2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide lists various methods tested in initial sprints for text extraction, including PaddleOCR, TesseractOCR, and others, but they did not yield the expected results.

slide_details.Text: For Consistency check:  Initially we were using the default LLM extraction from Dify Blocks only to check the consistency of documents. We were assigned two types of documents one was Interface and other was center document.. Interface had only .docx format data and center had both .docx and .xlsx format data After the completion of the extraction pipeline we used that pipeline here for consistency check it. was giving good results all the inconsistencies were highlighted and listed in the output from the LLM. O 2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The slide discusses using Dify Blocks' default LLM extraction to check the consistency of two document types: Interface (.docx) and center documents (.docx and .xlsx). The extraction pipeline successfully identified and highlighted inconsistencies in the documents.

slide_details.Text: Things we learnt from this project: based pipelines. Libreoffice should be avoided if possible (Dependency issues sometimes during deployment) ConvertAPI is an substitute but is paid. Dify can be used for chatbot and workflow orchestration: o It has good Ul for better usability. o There is a list of pre-built tools that can be used to make the process easier. o  It can be used in other places using its API. Azure Document Intelligence is a good choice for data extraction from Office documents. But it is suggested to use PDF format for better quality extraction.  2023 NTT DATA Corporation
slide_details.Slide_Summary: The project highlighted that LibreOffice has deployment issues and should be avoided, while ConvertAPI is a paid alternative. Dify is recommended for chatbot and workflow orchestration due to its user-friendly interface and pre-built tools, and Azure Document Intelligence is effective for data extraction from Office documents, preferably in PDF format for better results.

Presentation_Summary: The presentation details a project by NTT DATA focused on developing a robust data extraction pipeline for documents containing Japanese text, tables, and flowcharts. It outlines the challenges faced during data extraction from .docx and .xlsx files, including issues with merged cells and inconsistent formatting, and discusses various tools and methodologies explored, such as OCR techniques and the use of Azure Document Intelligence for improved accuracy and structure preservation. Ultimately, the project concluded with the deployment of a refined extraction pipeline that effectively handles document consistency checks while leveraging advanced AI models for enhanced performance.
